title: Density Weave Library and Rollout-State Contrast Audit for Cost Canvas
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Create a compact, responsive token subset (the 'Density Weave') and a clear mapping for rollout-state variants used across cost dashboards and rollout rails. Scope covers: metric cards, compact insight tiles, rollout rail states (canary, staged, rolled-back, deprecated), cost sparklines, compact filters, and the cost-explorer header. The outcome should: 1) unify spacing/typography scales for 3 density tiers (dense, normal, relaxed), 2) define color/opacity rules for rollout states with WCAG AA contrast targets, 3) provide a Figma library with component variants and usage guidance, and 4) hand off token JSON + migration notes for Eng to adopt in runtime CSS-in-JS and Console theme tokens. This ticket is primarily a design audit and prototype deliverable; engineering will consume the exported tokens and migration doc in follow-up ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library v1 published with component variants for metric-card, insight-tile, rollout-rail, and cost-header for three density tiers
Contrast spec documented for all rollout states that meets WCAG AA for normal text and AA Large for small numeric labels (include measured contrast ratios)
Token export (JSON and token key naming convention) pushed to the Design → Tokens Drive folder and linked in the ticket
Design review approvals from PM and two engineers (names in comments), and a short migration checklist for Eng
A/B prototype (Figma interactive) demonstrating density switch and rollout-state transitions shared with product team
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — scoped deliverables, identified primary components and stakeholders (PM: Jonathan Ruiz, Eng leads: Priya Shah, Omar Bello). Shared initial Figma frame with density token sketches.

2026-02-28 Marcus Nguyen: Completed first pass of density mapping (spacing/typography) and created dense/normal/relaxed variants for metric-card. Noted that small numeric labels at 10px in dense mode fail AA — need to either increase size or adjust weight/contrast.

2026-03-02 Priya Shah (Eng): Reviewed token naming. Asked for token keys to avoid camelCase collisions with runtime tokenizer. Requested explicit token fallbacks for Private deployments where theme overrides may be present. Added ENG-91802 as dependency.

2026-03-04 Accessibility review — Emma Li: Ran contrast checks against background surfaces. Results: canary state (#FF8A00 at 0.95 opacity on surface #0F1724) is 3.8:1 against body text — passes AA Large but not AA for 14px numerics. Recommendation: increase alpha to 1.0 for small numeric badges or add 1px outline token for small labels.

2026-03-06 Design sync: Decided to use a 'state-outline' token approach for dense small labels to preserve density without resizing typography. Logged trade-off: outline may slightly alter perceived color, documented in notes.
2026-03-09 Marcus Nguyen: Uploaded token export JSON to Drive and prototype with interactive density toggle. Linked PRD and left migration notes for ENG-92011.
2026-03-11 Jonathan Ruiz (PM): Reviewed prototypes and asked for two additional rollout-state visualizations: 'auto-fallback' and 'throttled-burst' — added scope to DES-314161.

2026-03-12 Design review: Requested approvals from Omar Bello and Emily Park. Omar left code-level suggestions around token naming conventions in comments; Emily approved visual language with minor copy tweaks.
decisions: Adopt three density tiers (dense / normal / relaxed) with explicit token suffixes: .density.dense | .density.normal | .density.relaxed
Use a combined approach for small numeric labels in rollout states: increase contrast via 'state-outline' token instead of increasing font-size in dense mode
Canonicalize rollout-state colors as semantically named tokens (state.success, state.warning, state.canary, state.deprecated) and provide 'state.alpha' variants for overlays
Ship Figma library v1 and token JSON together; engineering to pick up in ENG-92011 for runtime integration
